messages:
incident-bot: PAGE: GPU pool saturation in eu-west1 (severity=P1). Autoscaler is repeatedly failing to provision GPUs due to quota/limit denies. Queue length > 1200, client errors rising. PagerDuty: @maya oncall.

maya (oncall): I'm on it. seeing many createInstance RPC 403s in the autoscaler logs. starting triage.

luke (sre): quick note — autoscaler shows backoff loop: `scaleUp -> quotaDenied -> retry -> backoff` for ~15m. backlog is growing.

alice (cloud_ops): GCP console shows region quota for NVIDIA_T4 GPUs at 0 available until a quota increase is applied. Account-level quota also near cap. Opening support ticket but ETA > 2h.

sofia (support): we're already getting customer DMs about timeouts and grpc errors for realtime endpoints. Can we put a mitigation note on status.redwood.ai?

maya (oncall): yes, will draft status. But need immediate mitigation to reduce customer impact. Suggestions?

jonas (platform): can we route a subset of traffic to eu-west4 and us-central1 as fallback? We have warm pools there but not full capacity for current traffic.

kevin (eng-runtime): runtime can degrade model size to CPU-fallback for non-critical requests. We can also toggle aggressive prefix KV caching to reduce token churn for chat sessions. Both are quick toggles.

luke (sre): immediate plan I suggest: 1) divert non-SLA traffic to eu-west4, 2) scale down non-prod/elastic pools in eu-west1, 3) enable CPU-fallback routes for low-priority API keys.

alice (cloud_ops): I can mark non-prod projects for teardown to free up quota, but that only helps if quota is regional, and some quotas are per-account. filing support slack with GCP now — link: https://console.cloud.google.com/quotas?project=redwood-prod&region=eu-west1

maya (oncall): luke, can you run a quick script to pause canaries and reduce warm pool sizes? jonas, start reroute plan for eu-west4. kevin, prepare CPU-fallback toggle with a safe sampling.

luke (sre): running: `./scripts/scale-warmpools --region eu-west1 --shrink 40% --skip-critical` — monitoring. Logs: 
```
autoscaler: request createInstance gp-instance-xx -> quotaExceeded (403)
pool-manager: evicting noncritical warm nodes -> success
```

kevin (eng-runtime): prepping config change: `runtime.flags.cpu_fallback=true` for route tag `non_sla`. will ship with 5% sample then ramp if stable.

jonas (platform): reroute plan: update routing policy to prefer eu-west4 for models: text-gen-x, chat-legacy. Will keep eu-west1 as primary for SLA keys. Pushing route change in 30s.

pagerduty-bot: Reminder: Incident is acknowledged. Bridge: https://zoom.us/j/123456789 (open)

sofia (support): I've posted preliminary status update: "Intermittent timeouts for realtime endpoints in EU region. We're routing traffic and working with cloud provider; no data loss."
reactions: :loudspeaker: :hourglass_flowing_sand:

alice (cloud_ops): GCP support acknowledged ticket 987654321 — escalated to quota team. They say manual quota grant possible in ~90-120 minutes if we provide justification and expected usage.

maya (oncall): good. continuing mitigation. we need a quick customer-impact matrix: which customers are impacted and severity. sofia, can you collect top 5 by error rate?

sofia (support): on it. pulling from observability. preliminary: 3 customers >5% error rate, several more with latency spikes. I'll DM names to support oncall for handoff.

luke (sre): warmpool shrink completed. freed ~8 GPUs but backlog still high. Autoscaler retries still getting 403s for additional nodes.

kevin (eng-runtime): CPU-fallback sampling enabled at 5% for `non_sla` routes. initial telemetry: latency increased but error rate dropped for sampled requests.

jonas (platform): route change live. ~25% of non-SLA traffic now goes to eu-west4. monitoring for model compatibility issues.

sre_lead: prioritize customer comms for the 3 >5% impacted. if quota ETA is > 1h 30m we escalate to emergency preemptible burst in us-central as stopgap.

maya (oncall): agreed. alice, can you spin preemptible pools in us-central and eu-west4? even cross-region adds latency but reduces errors.

alice (cloud_ops): starting preemptible pool creation: `gcloud compute instances create --accelerator type=nvidia-t4,count=8 --preemptible --region=us-central1 ...` Will notify when up.

luke (sre): also adding a temporary rate limit for noisy tenants to protect core customers. pushing policy now.

sofia (support): customer comms: posted targeted emails to the top 3 customers and open Slack DMs. Asking if they'd like traffic rerouted to other regions.

incident-bot: Update: autoscaler backoff persists. Cloud Ops ticket updated: duplication of quota checks on our side flagged; working with GCP to confirm whether deny is actually account-level or project-level.

maya (oncall): next check-in in 10m. if preemptible pool spins up and traffic stabilizes we'll start de-escalation. keep notes in the incident doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/incidents/1768501234

kevin (eng-runtime): note for postmortem: we should have automatic reroute policy when regional quota denies exceed threshold for X minutes. current mapping is manual.

jonas (platform): agree — also need synthetic warm pools in secondary regions to avoid cold-starts when rerouting.

alice (cloud_ops): preemptible pool creation succeeded in us-central1, 16 T4s online. adding to capacity plane and testing routing.

luke (sre): I'm seeing backlog drop from 1200 -> 600 after reroute + preemptibles. request error rate trending down.

sofia (support): customers updated. some report improvement. keeping status page updated.

maya (oncall): thanks everyone. keep monitoring. we'll keep this thread open and do a full postmortem once quota resolution confirmed with GCP.

sre_lead: assign postmortem owners: luke (infra), kevin (runtime), jonas (routing), alice (cloud relations). 24h postmortem draft expected.

incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigated -> partial (traffic rerouted, preemptible capacity added). open actions: quota escalation follow-up, automated reroute runbook, postmortem.

maya (oncall): closing bridge in 20m if stable. tagging this incident for follow-up. :white_check_mark:
